_note: good.md, heading-quoted-and-nested.md, none-link.md, gate-good.md, gate-glob-good.md, gate-doc-only.md (a markdown file is not a gate file unless it is owner-only: gate-owner-markdown.md edits a skill and has no Gate changes section), gate-base-rule-good.md, gate-named-doc-good.md and gate-none.md, followup-filed.md, followup-in-code.md and followup-denied.md (it says no follow-ups and names /log-followup) pass. placeholder.md is the shipped PR template, unfilled: its example command and #123 live in comments and must not count. A `<name>.changes.json` beside a body lists what that PR changed; the gate-* cases are read against the harness's gate paths. A sidecar's `globs` are the gate paths the base branch's harness listed: a PR that removes a rule is held to it. One line may name a directory glob (`ci/fixtures/known-bad/p1/**`): it covers the files it matches and nothing else. A sidecar's `links` are the symlinks and submodule links the PR adds, removes or changes: each is a gate change (#149); a sidecar without that list is unreadable. gate-gitattributes.md and gate-gitmodules.md each change one of git's own settings files, which the harness guard counts and no harness rule names (#174), and have no Gate changes section. gate-named-doc.md changes the invariants document the base commit's AGENT.md names, a markdown file no harness rule names (#259): its sidecar's `globs` carries the path, and it has no Gate changes section; gate-named-doc-good.md is the same change with its line. A `<!--` closed by a `-->` beyond a heading may be a comment or two marks written as text, and the check cannot tell which, nor where a section ends (#189): the body gets that one finding and nothing else in it is read. gate-comment-mark.md has the marks in inline code and every gate file on its own line; gate-swallowed-heading.md has the same marks and names a gate file only in a later section; gate-hidden-section.md wraps its whole Gate changes section in a comment. part-of-open-unsaid.md says `Part of #31`, closes nothing, lists a run as not verified and says nothing about #31 staying open (#241): its finding leads with closing the issue the PR finished, then the owed section, then `leaves #n open`. part-of-owed.md (the section alone), part-of-leaves-open.md (the sentence alone) and part-of-closes.md (a closing link beside `Part of`) pass. part-of-leaves-other.md leaves open an issue it is not part of. part-of-bold-link.md writes its `Part of` in bold, with the issue as a link. part-of-quoted-answers.md only quotes its answers: a closing link in inline code and in an indented block, the sentence in inline code, the section inside a code block, and a closing word before #0. part-of-after-mark.md writes its `Part of` in a leading `---` block, above a comment opener and a one-line fence written as text, where a reader of prose alone would lose it; part-of-closes-and-leaves.md writes `#271 closes #252` in What and `leaves #252 open` under Links, as #288 did (#296): GitHub closes #252 on merge from the first sentence, whoever it is about, so P1 reports the issue once with both lines quoted and says how to write it. part-of-closes-other-leaves-open.md closes #12 and leaves #31 open: different numbers are no contradiction. The two sentences are read in the same forms and compared by repository as well as number (#323): part-of-closes-and-leaves-repo.md and part-of-closes-and-leaves-link.md write both in `owner/repo#n` and in a full issues link, part-of-closes-link-leaves-bare.md closes by link and leaves by bare number (a sentence with no repository may name the pull request's own, so it matches), and part-of-closes-repo-leaves-other-repo.md and part-of-closes-link-leaves-other-repo.md name the same number in different repositories and pass. part-of-closes-in-code-leaves-open.md has the closing word before #31 only in inline code, an indented block, a comment and a fence, and says in prose it leaves #31 open: it passes. prose-only.md says it leaves #4 open, so it keeps its one finding. followup-none-contradicted.md says Follow-ups is none and calls a deferred correction a follow-up in What (#242); followup-entry-unreferenced.md has one entry with an issue and one with neither an issue nor `not filed:`; followup-filed.md has one of each allowed form and still says follow-up in What; followup-in-code.md says follow-up only inside a code span and a code block. followup-denial-then-deferral.md writes no follow-up: and then names the work, with Follow-ups none; followup-nested-bullet.md defers work in a sub-bullet indented four spaces; followup-second-section.md has a second Follow-ups section whose entry names no issue and, since it repeats a heading, a repeated-heading finding too (#265). heading-repeated-cold-review.md writes Cold review three times (one in other case, with trailing spaces); heading-repeated-verification.md writes Verification twice, the second with no command, which the check used to read past; heading-quoted-and-nested.md passes: a Verification heading quoted in a fence, in a one-line comment and in an indented block, and one ### heading under two sections.
